evidence.field: 歲 / 形義通解; graph forms and senses, lines 173–179
evidence.text: The database says oracle-bone forms sometimes use 步 with 戉 as a phonetic element; it also presents a separate account in which 戉 was first borrowed to write 歲 and later differentiated with dots. It reports oracle-bone use for ‘year,’ citing Xu Zhongshu’s harvest-season explanation, and bronze examples for ‘years.’ It describes the seal graph as 从步、戌聲, reports later bronze forms with 月, and bamboo-slip forms with 日. It explains 歲星-to-year through Jupiter’s roughly twelve-year circuit. These are the database’s analyses; its summarized account does not establish a single uncontested origin or a continuous semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 歲

evidence.field: 戉 / 形義通解; early use and source-word limits
evidence.text: The database describes 戉 as an axe-like weapon graph and reports oracle-bone borrowing of 戉 for 歲, citing 合集 37849, 今戉(歲)受禾. This provides separate evidence for the graph’s weapon sense and its use for ‘year,’ but the page does not independently recover the spoken name of the depicted weapon; it therefore does not by itself prove that the weapon name supplied the sound of the year word.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 戉

evidence.field: 歲 / 形義通解; dated inscription references
evidence.text: The database cites oracle-bone use for ‘year’ and bronze examples: 敬事天王鐘「百歲之外」 and 蔡侯尊「冬(終)歲無疆」. It also says forms with 戌 as phonetic occur in the Juyan Han slips. The cited page does not give absolute dates for those individual artifacts or transcriptions, so these remain source-reported examples rather than independently dated attestations in this research.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 歲

evidence.field: 說文解字「歲」 entry and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The transmitted Shuowen entry defines 歲 as Jupiter, describes its passage across the twenty-eight lunar mansions and says it completes one circuit in twelve months; it analyzes the graph as 从步戌聲. Duan Yucai explains 步 as regular movement in the sky and additionally treats 戌 as associative. This is a historical lexicographic analysis, not direct proof of the earliest graph formation or earliest spoken sense.
evidence.title: 說文解字「歲」— Shuowen.org

evidence.field: File summary, original file link and licensing
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 歲-seal.svg as a vector depiction of 歲 in Shuowen seal-script style and links its stated source material to the Sinica database and Hanziyuan record S01196. It provides the original SVG link and declares the representation public domain. This is a modern digital redraw, not an image of an ancient artifact.
evidence.kind: glyph image provenance and rights record
evidence.title: File:歲-seal.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.text: The official lookup page states that per-ideograph Unihan records can include readings and other properties and directs users to query records by code point. The requested per-character endpoints for 岁 and 歲 could not be opened in this session, so no kMandarin value is attributed to inspected official character pages here.

evidence.text: Direct official endpoint attempted but inaccessible through the web tool. The provided local Unihan_Readings.txt rows state 岁 = suì and 歲 = suì, but those local rows are not emitted as external evidence and do not replace verification of the character pages.

evidence.text: Direct official endpoint attempted but inaccessible through the web tool. The supplied local Baxter–Sagart table gives 歲 Middle Chinese sjwejH and Old Chinese *s-qʷʰat-s. These local readings are recorded as local data only and are not independent external evidence for sound correspondence.

evidence.field: 歲 / historical readings and etymology discussion
evidence.text: The page lists competing reconstructions and word-origin proposals, including a proposed connection of 歲 with 越 ‘pass over,’ while noting alternative cycle-related derivation and unresolved morphology. Its displayed phonetic role for 戉 and reconstruction are not adopted as independently verified here: the provided local Baxter–Sagart data has a 歲 row only, with no supplied 戉 row, and CUHK does not independently reconstruct both in one system. Therefore no ancient sound match between a named weapon and 歲 is asserted.
evidence.title: 歲 — Wiktionary

evidence.field: 步 / 形義通解; graph and meaning of component
evidence.text: The database analyzes 步 as two 止 elements representing alternating feet and reports its basic sense as walking; it gives oracle-bone examples used for walking. This supports the semantic movement interpretation proposed for some 歲 forms, but does not establish that every early 歲 graph contains 步.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 步

search_audit.outcome: Inspected CUHK graph and component pages, Shuowen entry, Commons file description, and attempted Unicode endpoints. The per-character Unicode endpoints were inaccessible. Search surfaced divergent early-graph accounts.

search_audit.outcome: Search did not yield a relevant 歲 form record; opened generic Xiaoxuetang results, which did not establish a usable 歲 glyph candidate.

search_audit.query: 岁 simplified character derived cursive 歲 source 1956 simplification; site:unicode.org/reports/tr38 歲 岁 kMandarin Unicode Unihan
search_audit.outcome: Verified official Unihan lookup documentation but individual endpoint stayed inaccessible. Reviewed Wiktionary discussion of the cursive-derived simplified form and competing word etymologies; no primary simplification source located.

gaps: The earliest graph remains disputed: CUHK reports both early borrowing/differentiation from 戉 and variants analyzed with semantic 步 plus phonetic 戉; Shuowen later analyzes the seal graph as 步 + 戌. Primary inscription images and full contexts were not inspected, so a single original formation cannot be selected confidently.

The depicted weapon’s spoken name and pronunciation are not independently established here. A reconstruction for 歲 alone cannot establish the weapon-name-to-year-word sound match. The compound phonetic claim 戉 remains a source analysis without an independently checked paired reconstruction in one system.

The early sense trajectory is not continuous: ‘year’ examples and a harvest-season explanation are source-reported; Shuowen’s Jupiter definition and later year/age/harvest glosses do not by themselves establish the chronological semantic path. The dates of cited bronze artifacts and Juyan slips were not established from primary records in this pass.

The official per-character Unihan pages for 岁, 歲, 步, and 戉 remained inaccessible. Local readings were checked as supplied, but only 歲 has a supplied Baxter–Sagart row; no phonetic comparison is claimed.
Dong Chinese and Wiktionary were opened/reviewed but not used as primary support for the simplified-form lineage. The proposed cursive derivation of 岁 is not independently confirmed here.

The Commons image is a modern vector redraw. No ancient artifact photograph or securely sourced Xiaoxuetang glyph was selected. Bulk reuse of recurring database material was not evaluated or recommended; the single Commons file is public domain according to its exact file page.
